m.d: Snow is precipitation (falling water) that is white and frozen.
m.e: I like to ski on the snow.

m.d: A snow is a time when snow falls from the sky.
m.e: The snows of winter will soon come.

m.d: A shade of the color white.
If it is snowing, snow is coming down from the sky.
m.e: It snowed last night and everything is white now.

m.d: A snake is a long, thin reptile with no legs.
m.e: Some snakes will attack people, but most will try to hide or run away.

m.d: A snake is a dishonest, treacherous person.
m.e: Chuck is a snake to do a low thing like that.

m.d: A snake is a tool used to unclog plumbing.
If you snake, you move in a winding path.
m.e: The river snakes through the valley.

m.d: If you snake, you clean or unclog a clog using a plumbing snake.
An act of breaking something.
m.e: He snapped the ruler into two by accident.

m.d: If you sneak, you walk into a place quietly, usually to avoid being noticed by other people of that place.
m.e: The burglar sneaked into the room while we were sleeping and stole a bag of jewelries.

m.d: A snack is a small amount of food or a small meal.
m.e: The snacks I ate were potato chips and candy.

m.d: When you snack, you are eating a light meal.
m.e: While waiting for the movie to start, I snacked on some popcorn.

m.d: A sniper is a person using long-range weapons for precise attacks from a hidden position.
A snatch is a quick grab or catch.
If you snatch something from a person, you take it from them in a quick and rude way.
An act of breathing to find out what the smell is.
m.e: The dog sniffed the floor to find for any bones.

m.d: A snitch is a thief.
A snitch is someone who tells on the person about what they have done to try to get them in trouble; to tattle on a person.
If someone snitches on the person, they betray them by reporting them to the police or authorities
If someone snitches, they steal quickly and quietly.
If a person is sneaky, they are sly.
If a person is sneaky, they behave in a way that is difficult to detect.
Snoop is the act of snooping.
A snoop is a person who snoops.
If a person snoops, they spy or investigate someone secretly.
A sneeze, is a sudden blowing of air out of your nose and mouth because of a feeling in your nose.
m.e: She held her finger under her nose to stop a sneeze.

m.d: If you sneeze, a feeling in your nose makes you suddenly blow air out of your nose and mouth.
m.e: He sneezed until his nose was red.

m.d: A snail is a mollusc that moves very slowly. It has a shell on its back.
If a person is snappy, they are irritable and more likely to speak harshly.
A snappy person is someone who is tidy and sharp.
A snuff is powdered tobacco that is inhaled through the nose.
A snuff is the charred part of a candle wick.
If you snuff a candle, you extinguish it.
If you snuff, you inhale through the nose.
A snore is the act of snoring.
If a person or animal snores, they breathe during sleep with a harsh, snorting noises that is caused by an obstruction in air movement.
A snowy plot of land is covered with snow.
A snowman is a figure that looks like a human. It is made with large snowballs stacked on each other.
A snowball is a ball made of snow.
Snowball is something that gets out of control rapidly.
m.e: If you do not pay the bank on time, the interest will snowball.

m.d: A snort is the sound made by inhaling or exhaling roughly through the nose.
If a person snorts, they inhale or exhale roughly through the nose.
A snip is the action of cutting a small amount off something.
If you snip something, you use scissors and cut it with short and quick actions.
The snout is the front part of the head of a mammal.
m.e: Dogs have big snouts, but we have almost none.

m.d: A snuggle is an affectionate hug.
If you snuggle with someone, you lie close to them while hugging or being cozy.
A snooze is a brief period of sleep.
m.e: The cat enjoys taking a snooze on a sunny windowsill.

m.d: The snooze button on an alarm clock.
If you snooze, you sleep for a short period of time.
m.e: The boss caught him snoozing at his desk.

m.d: A snare is a trap that is used to catch small animals.
m.e: The snare caught a squirrel.

m.d: If something gets snared, it gets trapped in a snare.
m.e: The birds were snared.

m.d: A snowflake is a crystal of snow.
m.e: Look at all of the snowflakes falling on the driveway!

m.d: A snowstorm is a time when there is a lot of wind and snow in the air.
m.e: There was a big snowstorm that winter.

m.d: A snarl is the act of snarling.
If you snarl yourself, you get entangled in knots.
If you snarl someone, you place them in an embarrassing situation.
If a dog snarls, it growls angrily by showing its teeth.
A snicker is a laugh that is partially suppressed.
If a person snickers, they emit a snicker.
